tactics.claim: Choose a problem that hundreds of millions of people have, because only a small share of a market is in a buying window when you advertise, and a small market cannot scale no matter how well you execute.
tactics.mechanism: If only ~500K people would ever consider the product, ~95% of them are not ready to buy at any given time, so ad reach runs out. A market of 20M+ leaves enough in-window buyers to scale.

RSC already sells natural deodorant, body care, oral care and lip balm, which are all mass categories, so there is no market decision to make. The only translation is choosing which SKU leads paid acquisition, and existing offer-construction claims already cover that.

tactics.rejectReason: This is a category-selection decision RSC has already made in mass categories. The SKU-lead translation is already covered by offer-construction claims.

tactics.evidence: Assertion only.

tactics.claim: Under Meta's Andromeda update, creative is the targeting: hold one angle fixed and cross it with several distinct on-camera avatars (e.g. a 33-year-old high-performing woman and a 44-year-old suburban dad), so each avatar × angle pairing unlocks a different audience pocket.
tactics.mechanism: Andromeda routes delivery from the content of the creative. The person on screen acts as a mirror the viewer recognises themselves in, so the same angle carried by a different avatar is matched to a different audience rather than being clustered with the first ad.
tactics.evidence: Claims performance data from ~8,000 UGC ads shipped at Nibble; otherwise assertion.

rscFit.reasoning: This is a current (2026) platform mechanic, so age does not discount it. It applies directly to the live $50/day creative-test campaign, which already mixes his own creative with Trybe creator UGC. The honest scale-down is one angle × two or three avatars: his own face, an existing Trybe creator, and an AI-built character from the ai-broll workflow. Each creative is tagged by avatar and angle so delivery breakdowns can be read. It tensions with the existing claims to differentiate on pain angle and to aim at the shared center of the market. The reconciliation is that avatar is a delivery-diversity lever on a single fixed angle, not a separate message per demographic. That makes it complementary to the existing claim that Meta clusters near-identical creatives.

tactics.claim: Run a very steep subscription intro offer, e.g. $40 for month one on an $80 rebill (50% off the first order), to drive trial, then defend the second rebill through email and the habit formed in the first cycle.
tactics.mechanism: In consumables, trial is the bottleneck. A deep first-order price lowers the entry barrier and converts far more people into the subscription pool. The business makes its money on later full-price cycles, so the front end only has to acquire the customer.
tactics.evidence: Named brands (Gruns, Create Wellness, Instant Hydration, Mars Men, IM8) and the general subscription-brand playbook he plans to use; assertion.

rscFit.reasoning: This durable offer principle fits the binding constraint, conversion rate. The offer/AOV gate is open, so it can run today on the skin line only, where $15-25 contribution can absorb a first-order loss. It must not run on deodorant, soap, toothpaste or lip balm, which carry $2-5 contribution and would make every order negative. Merit is held at 5 on business risk: an 18-22.5% repeat rate means most deep-discount buyers would never reach a full-price refill. It overlaps the existing claim to price the front end and back end against different objectives, and it conflicts with the 'a discount only moves the effort/sacrifice term' claim. It should therefore be read as a skin-line subscription trial lever, checked against the measured second-order rate.

tactics.claim: Layer extremely cheap co-branded free gifts that the customer uses every day (a whisk, a mug, a frother, a ~$0.50 sleep mask, an onboarding kit) into the first order, both to lift conversion and to put the brand in front of the customer and their household every time the item is used.
